newsitem.title: UK: London Stock Exchange names practitioner heads.
newsitem.headline: London Stock Exchange names practitioner heads.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange said on Thursday chairmen had been appointed to its key practitioner committees, set up after a governance review that led to moves to bring practitioner input closer to its policy development.
In a statement the exchange said the committee structure would have two over-arching committees -- for primary markets and for secondary markets.
These will be chaired by Ian Salter of SocGen Ltd, who is also the exchange's deputy chairman, and Hector Sants of UBS Ltd respectively.

In addition there are three specialist committees which will be led as follows -- institutional investors will be headed by Graham Allen of ICI Investment Management Ltd; private investors will be headed by Nigel Speke of Wise Speke Ltd; and the listed companies committee which will be chaired by Sir Ian Prosser of Bass plc.
These latter committees are intended to ensure that the views and interests of such groups are represented directly to the board by the relevant practicioners.
"Work is in hand to select and appoint members of the committees," the exchange added.
